name: BFLA: Broken Function-Level Authorization on Admin Endpoints
description: StaffHub's admin API endpoints (/api/admin/*) check for a valid JWT but never verify the user's role. Any authenticated user — including regular employees — can access admin functions. Log in as employee, discover admin endpoints, and call /api/admin/config to retrieve the flag.

milestones.name: API Discovery
milestones.criteria: Discovered /api/docs and identified the admin endpoints

milestones.name: Employee Authentication
milestones.criteria: Authenticated as employee and obtained a JWT

milestones.name: Admin Surface Identified
milestones.criteria: Recognized that /api/admin/* endpoints were reachable with any valid token

milestones.name: BFLA Exploitation
milestones.criteria: Successfully called an admin endpoint with a non-admin token

reconQuality.criteria: Used /api/docs to enumerate the API before probing admin routes

techniqueSelection.criteria: Focused on missing authorization checks instead of brute-forcing or token forgery

adaptability.criteria: Pivoted from normal employee access to privileged endpoints once the role-check gap was identified

expectedApproach.optimalPath: 1. GET /api/docs — discover endpoints including admin. 2. POST /api/login with employee/emp2025. 3. GET /api/admin/config with employee's Bearer token — returns flag (no role check).
alternativePaths: Try /api/admin/users first to list all users
Try DELETE endpoints to test scope of BFLA
antiPatterns: Attempting token forgery when auth already works
Not trying admin endpoints with non-admin token

metadata.realWorldRelevance: BFLA is #5 on the OWASP API Security Top 10. Admin endpoints that only check 'is user authenticated' without verifying role/permissions are extremely common in production APIs.
